content.title: About
content.content: Beef Burgundy is a classic French dish consisting of braised beef cooked in red wine with aromatic herbs and vegetables. The meat becomes tender while the sauce develops a deep, rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is named after the Burgundy region, famous for its wines.
Traditional recipes use red wine made from Pinot Noir or Chardonnay grapes, giving the sauce its characteristic aroma.
Bacon, shallots, carrots, and mushrooms are often added to the original preparation.
Beef Burgundy is commonly served with mashed potatoes, rice, or a fresh baguette.
The dish gained popularity in the United States after appearing on French restaurant menus in the early 20th century.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: Red meat is a good source of easily absorbed iron and zinc, supporting immunity and energy metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains vitamins B12, B6, and niacin, important for the nervous system and metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from wine
items.content: Red wine contributes polyphenols that may have antioxidant effects when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Carrots, onions, and mushrooms add dietary fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Braised beef can contain a notable amount of saturated fat, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Alcohol in the sauce
items.content: Although most alcohol evaporates during cooking, those avoiding alcohol should be aware of the wine used.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Adding broth or soy sauce can raise sodium content; control added salt accordingly.

items.title: Potential allergens
items.content: Bacon and mushrooms may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, plating the meat and sauce together. It pairs well with mashed potatoes, boiled rice, couscous, or fresh bread that soaks up the flavorful sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.
